fr:mainmatter.html:p: Part of Modern Web Browser from Within Emacs.

Lean 4's ProofWidgets4 library lets tactics render interactive UI — clickable terms, goal diagrams, drag-and-drop rewrites — as part of the tactic state. The official Lean VSCode extension hosts these widgets in a WebView, which is effectively an embedded Chromium capable of running the widget's React components.

lean4-mode for Emacs does not currently support proof widgets: it receives the widget payload over LSP but has no way to render arbitrary React/HTML. This is the main interactive-proof feature that keeps users tethered to VSCode.

Hypothesis: if Emacs can host a real browser surface (e.g. EAF or xwidget-webkit, per the parent tree), lean4-mode could shell the widget HTML/JS out to that surface and regain feature parity with VSCode.

html:ul.html:li: What exactly does the Lean LSP send for a widget? Serialized React element tree, or a URL to a bundled component? (Check the Lsp.InteractiveGoal schema and the widget RPC.)
Does the widget runtime assume VSCode-specific APIs (postMessage bridge, vscode.d.ts bindings)? If so, we'd need a shim.
Can we render widgets in a side buffer that updates as the cursor moves, or do they need to be inline with the goal view?
Is there already prior art — an abandoned branch, an issue thread on leanprover-community/lean4-mode, or a proof-of-concept in Doom/Spacemacs land?

fr:title.text: Modern Web Browser from Within Emacs

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Modern Web Browser from Within Emacs

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Investigate embedding a modern web browser (full HTML/CSS/JS, not just eww) inside Emacs. Candidates include emacs-application-framework (EAF), xwidget-webkit, and similar WebKit-based options.

html:ul.html:li: Stay in Emacs. Browsing the web without leaving the editor keeps keybindings, buffer management, and workflow consistent.

Lean proof widgets. Running a real React-capable renderer inside Emacs would let lean-mode display the interactive proof widgets that are currently Lean-exclusive to VSCode. See Lean Proof Widgets in Emacs.

Rich forest rendering. Replace the plain-text tree preview with a proper rendering of the compiled Forester HTML (math, transclusions, layouts, Datalog query results). See Rich Forest Rendering in Emacs.

EAF vs. xwidget-webkit: which is more maintainable on macOS? EAF requires a Python backend and a compatible Qt/WebEngine; xwidget-webkit needs Emacs built with the --with-xwidgets flag, which is not default in Homebrew builds.
How much of this can be done with a headless render + image display instead of a live embedded browser? For static forest previews that may be enough; proof widgets need a live JS runtime.
Security posture: an embedded browser running arbitrary JS inside Emacs has a bigger blast radius than a normal editor. Should it be sandboxed or scoped to local URLs only?
